newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices hold amid continuing heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices hold amid continuing heat.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were mostly steady Wednesday as warmer-than-normal weather throughout most of the U.S. continued to keep air conditioners cranking, market sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices remained in the high-$2.20s to low-$2.30s per mmBtu, while south Texas prices also held in the low-$2.20s.
Temperature highs in Houston over the next few days are expected hover around 90 degrees F, Weather Services Corp reported.
In the East, New York city gate prices soared early into the high-$2.60s to about $2.70, but as futures faltered prices dove into the high-$2.50s, traders said.
A brief spell of cooler weather is forecast to arrive in the Northeast Friday, but warmer-than-normal weather is expected to return by the weekend, according to WSC.
In the Midwest, where a similar weather pattern was forecast, prices also held onto $2.10-2.13. Chicago city-gate prices were quoted in the low-$2.40s.
In West Texas, Permian prices failed to budge from $2.07-2.12, while southern California border prices also remained strong at $2.26-2.28.
Separately, injection estimates for today's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 70 to 100 bcf, with most at 85-90 bcf. This compares with a gain of 91 bcf a year ago.
